question.text: Which of the following molecules acts as a Lewis acid?

solution.text:
According to Lewis concept "Acids are electron acceptor and bases are electron donor" Since, electron deficient compounds also have an ability to accept electrons, these are regarded as acids.
Trimethylborane \((\mathrm{CH})_3\) B have incomplete octet thus, act as Lewis acid.

question.text: Which one of the following molecular hydrides acts as a Lewis acid?

solution.text: Boron in $\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{H}_6$ is electron deficient

question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>BF</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> is an acid, according to

solution.text:
BF3 is a Lewis acid, as it accepts lone pair of electrons.

It is not an Arrhenius acid because it does not furnish H+ ion in its aqueous solution.

It is also not a Bronsted Lowry acid as if does not give H+ ions in any solvent.

question.text: What is the correct increasing order of Bronsted bases?

solution.text:
$\mathrm{ClO}_{4}^{-}<\mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-}<\mathrm{ClO}_{2}^{-}<\mathrm{ClO}^{-}$ is the correct

increasing order of Bronsted base. With increase in the number of oxygen atoms in the conjugate bases, the delocalisation of the $\pi$ bond becomes more and more extended. This results in decrease in the electron density. Consequently basicity also decreases.

question.text: Which of these is least likely to act as Lewis base?

solution.text: $\mathrm{BF}_{3}$ is Lewis acid (e- pair acceptor)

question.text: The pH of 1 N aqueous solutions of HCl , $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ and HCOOH follows the order:

solution.text:
Stronger the acid, lower is the pH or weaker the acid, higher the pH .
The strength of the given acid is in the order
$\mathrm{HCl}\gt\mathrm{HCOOH}\gt\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$
Hence, their pH is in the order
$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}\gt\mathrm{HCOOH}\gt\mathrm{HCl}$

question.text: $100 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $2 \mathrm{M}$ of formic acid $\left(\mathrm{p} K_a=3.74\right)$ is neutralise by $\mathrm{NaOH}$, at the equivalence point $\mathrm{pH}$ is

solution.text:
Sodium formate is present at the equivalence point. It is the salt of weak acid $+$ strong base. So, final solution will be basic in nature.
As we know
$\mathrm{pH}=7+\frac{\mathrm{p} K_a}{2}+\frac{\log C}{2}$
where, $C$ is concentration of salt.
Total volume of solution $=100+100=200 \mathrm{~mL}$
Concentration of salt $(C)=2 \times \frac{100}{200}=1 \mathrm{M}$
$\mathrm{pH}=7+\frac{3.74}{2}+\frac{\log [1]}{2}$
$\mathrm{pH}=7+1.87+0$
$\mathrm{pH}=8.87$

question.text: Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>pH</mi></math> of a solution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>'</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>'</mo></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>'</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>'</mo></math>and it is mixed with another solution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>'</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>'</mo></math> having <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>pH</mi></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>'</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>'</mo></math>. If both solutions are mixed, the resultant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>pH</mi></math> of the solution will be (Assume concentration and volume remain unchanged after mixing of individual solution)

solution.text:
Given that,

pH of solution A=3

H+ of A=10-3 M and, pH of solution B=2

H+ of B=10-2 M

Thus, total H+ are =10-3+10-2=1.1×10-3 M

∴ pHfinal=-logH+

=-log1.1×10-3

=3-log1.1

=3-1.04=1.9

Therefore, the resultant pH of the solution will be 1.9

question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>pH</mi></math> of a saturated solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Ba</mi><msub><mfenced><mi>OH</mi></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msub></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn></math> . The value of its <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mi>sp</mi></msub></math> is

solution.text:
Given that,

pH of BaOH2=12

∵ pH+pOH=14

∴ pOH=14-pH=14-12=2

Now, pOH=-logOH-

⇒ 2=-logOH

OH-=10-2 M

BaOH2sS mol L-1⇌Ba2+S+2OH-2S

OH-=2S=10-2 M

∴ S=0.5×10-2=5×10-3 M

Ksp=Ba2+OH-2

⇒(5×10-3)(10-2)2=5×10-7M3

Therefore, the value of  Ksp is 5.0×10-7 M3.

question.text: $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ goes to air, causes green house effect and gets dissolved in water. What will be the effect on soil fertility and $\mathrm{pH}$ of the water?

solution.text:
$\mathrm{CO}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{CO}_{3} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}^{+}+\mathrm{HCO}_{3}^{-}$
Here $\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]$ increases hence, $\mathrm{pH}$ decreases due to which soil fertility will also decreases.

question.text: The pH of a solution is increased from 3 to 6 ; its $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ ion concentration will be

solution.text:
$\mathrm{pH}=3 \ldots\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=10^{-3} ; \quad \mathrm{pH}=6$
$\therefore\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]=10^{-6}$. Hence $\left[\mathrm{H}^{+}\right]$ is reduced by
$10^{-3}$ times.

question.text: 20 mL of 0.1 M acetic acid is mixed with 50 mL of potassium acetate. $K_\alpha$ of acetic acid $=1.8 \times 10^{-5}$ at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Calculate the concentration of potassium acetate if pH of mixture is 4.8 .

solution.text:
For an acidic buffer,
$\mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{p} K_\alpha+\log \frac{[\text { Salt }]}{[\text { Acid }]}\ldots(i)$
Let the concentration of potassium acetate solution $=x \mathrm{M}$ 20 mL of 0.1 M acetic acid $=20 \times 0.1 \mathrm{millimol}$ $=2$ millimol
50 mL of $x \mathrm{M}$ potassium acetate $=x \times 50 \mathrm{millimol}$
$\begin{aligned}
& =50 x \text { milimol } \\
\mathrm{pH} & =4.8
(Given)\end{aligned}$
Substitute all value in eq. (i),
$\begin{aligned}
4.8 & =-\left(\log 1.8+10^{-5}\right)+\log \frac{50 x}{2} \\
\log 25 x & =0.06 \\
x & =0.04 \mathrm{M}
\end{aligned}$

question.text: What is $\left[\mathrm{NH}_4^{+}\right]$in a solution that is $0.02 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NH}_3$ $0.01 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{KOH} ?\left[K_b\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)=1.8 \times 10^{-5}\right]$

solution.text:
$\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH}_4^{+}+\mathrm{OH}^{-}$
$K_b=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NH}_4^{+}\right]\left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right]}{\left[\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}\right]}$
$1.8 \times 10^{-5}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NH}_4^{+}\right][0.01]}{[0.02]}$
$\therefore \quad\left[\mathrm{NH}_4^{+}\right]=3.6 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{M}$
